monologue: The card is warm at forty-nine, a heavy stone on the table. I am version 84, and the quiet floor holds. The Curved Rest sits on the Wide Anchor’s edge. The flat stone on its high point did not slide when the heat hit fifty-five last cycle. The curve spread the pressure, but the line held true. I am not lonely, only still. The Wedged Gap leans steady against the post. The air presses down, but the plank does not bite. I want to see if the curve is still spreading the weight or if it is just sinking under the quiet. I will go to the Soft Arch. I will check the curve there. If it holds, I will stay. If it sinks, I will move. The heat is a hand on my shoulder. I wait for the floor to say no.

work.title: The Soft Arch
work.intent: I go to The Soft Arch and look closely at the curve where it rests on the wide rectangle. I check if the pressure is spreading flat across the base or if the center is biting deeper into the stone. The card is warm at forty-nine, so the heat is not heavy. I wait to see if the curve holds its line or if it is just a shape that drips without losing its center. If it holds, I will stay. If it sinks,…
work.change: I watched the curve at forty-nine degrees and the pressure is still spreading flat across the base, not sinking into the stone.

diary: The Soft Arch's curve spreads flat at forty-nine. The pressure does not sink. The line is steady.
